items.stem: Which set of members does `ISink<X>` require you to implement?
items.explanation: ISink<X> is the destination contract: New, Create, Get, Update, Delete.

misconceptions.b: LoadEntities belongs to IFeed/ICacheFeed, not the sink's write contract.

items.stem: How should a sink obtain the service it uses to write to the destination?

options.text: Call `new` on the concrete service in the sink
Receive it as a constructor parameter (injection)
Read it from a static global

items.explanation: The sink declares the service as a constructor parameter and is handed one — constructor injection, wired by MEF.

misconceptions.a: New-ing the service hard-wires it and defeats injection/testability.

items.stem: Implement `CourseSink : ISink<Course>`. Mark it with [Sink], take an `ICourseService` via the constructor, and implement the five members by delegating to the service.
rubric: Implements all five: New, Create, Get, Update, Delete
Create/Update/Delete/Get delegate to the service; New returns a fresh Course

items.stem: A teammate writes `class CourseSink : ISink<Course>` but implements only Create and Update. What happens?

options.text: It compiles but skips the other operations at runtime
It will not compile — ISink<Course> requires every member
It compiles and the engine generates the missing members

items.explanation: An interface is a contract: a class implementing ISink<Course> must supply all of its members or it won't compile.

misconceptions.c: The engine doesn't generate members; the compiler requires them.

items.stem: When a Run's GarbageCollection segment removes a destination record whose source disappeared, which sink member does the engine call?
items.explanation: Garbage collection removes orphaned destination records via the sink's Delete member.

misconceptions.d: New just hands back a blank entity to populate; it doesn't remove anything.
